cards.text: Israel's on the road through the wilderness. The whole congregation sets out from Kadesh and comes to Mount Hor. The WHOLE congregation, friend, which makes the Millers' kitchen on birthday-batch day look like a quiet afternoon.

cards.question: Mount Hor sits right near the border of another land. Which one?

cards.text: There at Mount Hor, the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, Israel's priest. And God says Aaron will be gathered to his people.

cards.question: God tells Moses and Aaron that Aaron will enter the land He has given the Israelites.

cards.text: God doesn't leave Aaron guessing why. He gives the reason, and it goes all the way back to the waters of Meribah.

cards.question: God says Aaron was the only one at fault at the waters of Meribah.
God says both Moses and Aaron did something at the waters of Meribah. What was it?

cards.text: Then God gives Moses the plan. Take Aaron up Mount Hor, and bring one of Aaron's sons along too.

cards.question: God tells Moses to take Aaron and his son ___ up Mount Hor.
Up on Mount Hor, God tells Moses to take something off Aaron the priest and put it on Eleazar. What is it?

cards.text: God says it plainly: Aaron will die there. And Moses does as the LORD commanded. I bet that was the longest climb of his life.

cards.question: Moses, Aaron and Eleazar climb Mount Hor where nobody can see them.

cards.text: At the top, Moses removes Aaron's garments and puts them on Eleazar. Then Aaron dies there, on top of the mountain.

cards.question: After Aaron dies on top of Mount Hor, who comes back down the mountain?

cards.text: Down below, the whole congregation sees that Aaron has died. And the entire house of Israel mourns for him.

cards.question: The entire house of Israel mourns for Aaron for ___ days.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to 'the Millers' kitchen on birthday-batch day,' but nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up. Only the junk drawer is known from onboarding. Without a setup, the comparison may not land for a baker.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: 'It goes all the way back to the waters of Meribah' makes Meribah sound long ago. The text gives no time, and the Meribah events are earlier in this same chapter (Num 20:13).

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Card 5 names Meribah but never says what happened there. A baker who hasn't read the passage before can't reason between 'Rebelled against His command,' 'Ran away from the people' and 'Forgot to give Him thanks.' Card 5 needs a short line of context from Numbers 20 (for example, that something happened when water came from the rock), or the question needs to change.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: No earlier card hints whether the climb was public or private, so this true or false is a coin flip. Card 11 could set up the moment, for example by turning toward the people watching below, so the baker has something to reason from.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Cards 3, 8, 13 and 15 are plain retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Outside card 1's callback and card 11's 'I bet' line, the stop reads like a flat summary. The passage is solemn, so big jokes may not fit, but warmth, a storyteller's line or a quiet guess at a feeling marked as his own would still keep him present.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
